newsitem.title: BENIN: EMU will not change France's CFA role - minister.
newsitem.headline: EMU will not change France's CFA role - minister.

text.p: European monetary union will not affect France's cooperation with the African Franc Zone (CFA) which links 14 countries through a common currency, French Overseas Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain said on Thursday.
He told CFA finance ministers at a meeting in the Benin capital, "When the French franc is replaced by the Euro, no change in the parity of the CFA franc will be necessary."
The CFA franc is linked to the French franc at a fixed rate and member countries agree to keep their reserves mainly in French francs.
The one-day meeting was due to confirm Portuguese-speaking Guinea-Bissau's switch to the CFA franc from the peso from May 2.
French Economics Minister Jean Artuis said economic growth in the CFA was about five percent in 1996 compared with 4.8 percent in 1995, still too low to attract private investment.
The meeting was due to confirm a charter aimed at encouraging private investment in the currency zone.

Its 30 recommendations include strict budgetary and monetary policies to reform and harmonise tax structures, a clear legal framework for economic activity, improved infrastructure and a war against corruption.
The zone now comprises Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Congo, the Comoros, the Central African Republic, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Ivory Coast, Mali, Chad, Togo, Niger and Senegal. ($1=579 CFA)
